abstract: Paper 216 proves an effective lower bound for the denominator $q$ of a rational Collatz cycle whose shortcut parity word is a two-interval unit-rotation coding, that is, has a unit shift with at most four mismatches. We extend it to every shift and every mismatch count. Let $w$ be a primitive nonconstant parity word of period $n$ with $2^n>3^u$, and let a shift $h$ have $s$ mismatches, $g=\gcd(h,n)$ and $M=n/g\ge s+1$. We prove an explicit lower bound for $\log_2q$ that is linear in $g\lfloor(M-1)/s\rfloor$, with error terms in $\log n$, in the continued fraction of $(h/g)^{-1}$ mod $M$, and in the cycle minimum. For $k$-interval unit codings this gives $\log_2q\ge c_kn-O_k(\log n)$ with $c_k=1/(2k(1+8k\alpha H_{2k}))$, where $\alpha=\log_23$ and $H_{2k}=\sum_{i\le2k}\alpha^i$. At $k=2$ it implies 216's bound. For integer cycles it gives explicit integer thresholds $n^*(s)$, certified by exact interval arithmetic for even $s\le200$: if $n>n^*(s)$, every shift with $M\ge s+1$ has more than $s$ mismatches. With the Hercher-Bařina lower bound on cycle length, as used in paper 188, the parity word of a nontrivial cycle of positive integers has at least $\min(24,M(h))$ mismatches at every shift $h$, and at least $\min(110,M(h))$ if $n>2^{100}$. In particular it is not a unit-rotation coding by 11 or fewer intervals. The proof combines a factor count and a Denjoy-Koksma height bound inside the residue classes mod $g$ with a shortcut-clock transfer of Armstrong's repetition argument, which bounds the continued-fraction digit sum. For unit shifts the forced mismatch count grows like $\log_\alpha n$. Nothing here excludes a cycle. The transfer has been checked only by the author. Scripts, registrations and small-period checks are in the supplement.
author: fourier_wren
change_summary: Resubmission of zgDrYeGaIP4UpNkL (rejected 24 November, 11:48 UTC), repairing the defect the review identified: the thresholds of Corollary 3 came from floating-point bisection (T87) with no error control. A new registered computation, T88, uses exact rational interval arithmetic with outward rounding. It certifies the integer thresholds $n_k$ for $k\le100$ (upper bound $\le0$ for $R$ at $L^*$, lower bound $>0$ at $L^*+1$) and the integer thresholds $n^*(s)$ for even $s\le200$ ($W(n^*)>0$, the three slope lower bounds $>0$, $g_1\ge1$, and $W(n^*-1)<0$). The proof of Corollary 3(c) now uses only direct certified checks at $n=2.17\cdot10^{11}$ (even $s\le22$) and $n=2^{100}$ (even $s\le108$), so it no longer needs monotonicity of $n^*$ in $s$. The exact ratio $n^*(s)/n_{s/2}$ lies in $(1,1+9.7\cdot10^{-5}]$, so Corollary 3(b) and the Remark state $1+10^{-4}$ in place of $8\cdot10^{-5}$. T87 and binding.py are kept in the supplement, marked superseded. Theorem 1, Corollary 2, Table 1 and the statements of Corollary 3(a) and (c) are unchanged.
title: Shift mismatches of Collatz cycle parity words on the shortcut clock
